title.narrative: Activity under preparation Nature Conservation and Sustainable Land Governance in Ethiopia

description.narrative: Contract related to: Nature Conservation and Sustainable Land Governance in Ethiopia - Ethiopia hosts some of Africa¿s most biodiversity-rich landscapes, crucial, among other things, for climate regulation, carbon sequestration, and ecosystem services. However, deforestation, habitat loss, and land degradation, driven by weak governance, unregulated land use and population growth and conflict, are threatening the wellbeing of its natural heritage. The country¿s policy framework prioritizes biodiversity conservation and climate resilience through initiatives such as the Climate-Resilient Green Economy (CRGE) Strategy, National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP), and Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), aligning with EU strategies, like the EU Biodiversity Strategy for 2030, and NaturAfrica Programme. Ethiopia is also engaged in the implementation of African Union¿s Great Green Wall Initiative to combat desertification.The Action focuses on three conflict-affected landscapes in Northern Ethiopia: Simien Mountains, Desa¿a Forest, and Hallaideghe Plain, spanning Afar, Tigray, and Amhara regions. These landscapes are indicative and selected for their exceptionally rich biodiversity potential, critical role in water regulation and carbon storage, and their vulnerability to climate change, worsened by land use conflict, leading to encroachment, deforestation, overgrazing and land degradation. The Simien Mountains have lost 35,000 hectares of forest over the past two decades, facing severe soil erosion and climate-induced degradation, though initiatives like the Grazing Pressure Reduction Strategy (GPRS) have helped mitigate overgrazing. Desa¿a Forest has seen a 40% reduction in dense forest cover since 1972 due to illegal logging, encroachment, and recurrent droughts, while resource conflicts between Tigray farmers and Afar pastoralists remain a significant challenge. Hallaideghe Grasslands suffer from overgrazing, water shortages, and rangeland degradation, threatening both wildlife and pastoralist livelihoods.Local communities in these landscapes depend heavily on natural resources for their survival, hence adopting sustainable land management, and alternative livelihood measures such as green businesses, are essential for both economic development and biodiversity conservation. The Action will work to balance ecological preservation with community needs by promoting sustainable resource use and strengthening economic opportunities that align with environmental protection.The Action responds to the urgent need for recovery, rebuilding, and stabilization in Northern Ethiopia while addressing critical challenges related to biodiversity loss, climate change mitigation, and household resilience. Aligned with Ethiopia¿s Resilient Recovery and Reconstruction Framework (3RF) 2023-2028, the intervention promotes the Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus (HDPN) approach, ensuring that conservation efforts support both environmental sustainability and community livelihoods. Given the ongoing insecurity in the targeted regions, a conflict-sensitive approach will be applied, with the final selection of indicative landscapes determined through security assessments to ensure feasibility. The Action will promote nature-based solutions, integrating ecosystem restoration, sustainable resource management, and green investments to strengthen climate resilience and local economies. This strategy will also lay the groundwork for improved conditions under the EU¿s Global Gateway priorities, demonstrating how biodiversity conservation can drive climate-resilient economic development while fostering long-term stability in vulnerable landscapes.
